name: Push history entries (back button limits)
plain: Adds fake history entries so Back does less than expected; browsers skip entries made without a click.
meaning: A site can change the address bar and history without loading a page. Misused, it traps the back button and keeps the person on the site, so browsers now skip entries added with no user interaction.

access.persistence: Entries live in the tab session history
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Same-origin URLs only; cross-origin frames affect the joint session history of the tab
steps: Call pushState with a same-origin URL
Back button or Navigation API fires popstate

limits.headline: Can add extra Back button steps, but browsers skip steps made without a tap
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as you move around the page, or after your first tap.
can: Change the address bar to a new page address without a full reload
Add steps so Back goes to a screen inside the app
Keep the Back button working in apps that load pages without reloading
cannot: Trap you for good on a page, because browsers skip steps made without a click or tap
Change the address to a different website
Hide where you actually are from the browser
Block you from leaving through the address bar or a bookmark

story.what_it_is: A site can add steps to your Back button list, and sometimes abuse it.

marketing.name: History API
marketing.pitch: MDN says pushState lets a page change the address bar and history without reloading.

story.for_you: When you move around a single page app, the address changes and Back works as you would expect. On bad sites, Back may seem broken because the page piled up extra entries.
story.for_makers: Single page apps use it to give each view its own link without reloading. Shady sites use it to trap people, so browsers now skip entries made without a click.

use_cases.example: Scrolling a feed and tapping a post gives a new address, so Back returns you to the feed.
A product filter updates the URL so you can share the filtered list.
Opening a document in a web app gives it its own link without a full page load.
Some ad pages stuff the Back list so that pressing Back leads to another ad page.
A streaming site opens a title in a panel and still lets Back close it.
Analytics tools watch history changes to count a new page view in single page apps.

technical_bounds: URL must be same origin as the document (SecurityError otherwise); no cross-origin path spoofing
Chrome 75 history manipulation intervention: entries added by pages that had no user interaction are skipped by Back and the long-press history menu
State object serialized size limit about 16 MiB in Firefox (browser.history.maxStateObjectSize 16 MiB); Chrome has no fixed limit but is IPC bound
Rate limits: Safari throws SecurityError after about 100 calls in 30 s; Firefox after about 200 calls in 10 s; Chrome throttles flood of navigations
Page cannot read other sites' history entries or the length beyond history.length (capped at 50 in Chrome, 50 to 1000 depending on browser)

history.change: History manipulation intervention: skip entries without user activation
Navigation API ships with entries() same-origin only
Chrome documents back-button hijacking as a spam behavior in Search and tightens intervention coverage (verify current status)
